newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks keep firm grip on gains to noon.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks keep firm grip on gains to noon.

text.p: SPI Futures 2477 +28 US 30yr cl 7.04 -0.05
10yrbond futs 92.195 +0.025 Gold NY 341.35 Lon fix 341.60
AUD US$0.7775 (Tue 0.7760) CRB Index cl 246.54 -1.07
*Stocks keep grip on Dow-inspired gains to midsession after inflation data meets expectations. Volume 199.33 million, value A$358.66 million, 855 stocks traded, 265 steady, 417 up, 173 down.
Australian shares kept a firm rip on their Dow-inspired gains to the midsession on Wednesday with March quarter inflation data meeting market expectations.
By 12.00 p.m. (0210 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 24.1 points at 2,471.7. June share price index futures were 28 points higher at 2,477, a 5.3 point premium to the index.

The market had no trouble digesting a 0.2 percent increase in the annual inflation rate to 1.3 percent and an increase of 0.4 percent to 2.1 percent for Treasury's measure of underlying inflation. Having seen the much-anticipated figures, the focus quickly returned to the strength in offshore markets.
"It was virtually as was expected," said dealer Brett O'Donovan of Brisbane-based brokerage, Lance Jones, adding that while bonds had dipped on the figure, the stock market had seen little impact.
"The bonds moved a little bit but equities didn't follow. Our market is really focussing on what is happening overseas."
Rises were across the board with the blue chips finding plenty of interest from investors inspired by Wall Street.
National Australia Bank saw most interest among the majors with just over three million shares traded by midday. Australia's largest bank was up 17 cents to A$17.04.
Outside the leaders, West Australian regional Bankwest was up a cent to A$2.53 by the midsession after it posted a full year net profit of A$94.5 million.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about five to two, while about 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
In other local markets, the Australian dollar recouped 1/4 cent of early losses at the midsession after inflation data were not so weak as to greatly raise the risk of a rate cut.
By 12.25 p.m. (0225 GMT), the dollar had scampered back up to US$0.7765/70 having slid to US$0.7745/50 just before the data hit dealing screens from an early US$0.7770/75.
Australian bond yields rebounded from their initial lows after a pretty benign March quarter inflation report was not weak enough for the market to rally further.
By 12.35 p.m. (0235 GMT), 10 year T-Bonds were yielding 7.82 percent, steady with Tuesday's close.
